paragraphs.text: Mania with spouse collateral, declined then accepted medication

paragraphs.label: Patient's words
paragraphs.text: The patient does not provide a main complaint and states, "I do not know why I am here."

sections.heading: 3. History of Present Illness / Current Episode

paragraphs.label: Primary reason for treatment
paragraphs.text: The patient reports not knowing why they are at the clinic.

paragraphs.label: Duration of current episode
paragraphs.text: The patient reports symptoms for ten days.

paragraphs.label: Functional impact
paragraphs.text: The patient reports spending a lot of money, buying a used truck for eleven thousand dollars, and being irritable with the kids.

paragraphs.label: Narrative / additional details
paragraphs.text: The patient reports not needing sleep, having a lot of energy, and having many ideas. The spouse reports the patient has been talking very fast. The patient had a similar episode in 2019 and was hospitalized for nine days. The patient denies thoughts of hurting themselves or others. The patient smokes marijuana almost every day and has a penicillin allergy. The patient initially refuses medication but agrees to try olanzapine and to participate in a partial hospitalization program.

The patient reports experiencing elevated mood, increased energy, and racing thoughts, along with a reduced need for sleep for the past ten days. The patient also mentions having a history of a similar episode in 2019 that lasted nine days. The spouse reports the patient has been spending money impulsively and has been irritable with the children.
The patient denies any thoughts of hurting themselves or others.

paragraphs.label: Prior hospitalizations
paragraphs.text: The patient reports one prior psychiatric hospitalization in 2019 for nine days.

paragraphs.label: Prior suicide attempts / self-harm
paragraphs.text: The patient denies prior suicide attempts or self-harm.

paragraphs.label: Prior medications and response
paragraphs.text: The patient reports receiving lithium during the prior hospitalization but stopped taking it after a few months as they felt fine.

sections.heading: 6. Suicide Risk Assessment - Columbia / C-SSRS Documentation Area

paragraphs.label: Substances and pattern
paragraphs.text: The patient reports smoking marijuana almost every day, maybe a gram.

paragraphs.label: Medical history
paragraphs.text: The patient reports a history of a manic episode in 2019 for which they were hospitalized for nine days.

paragraphs.label: Allergies
paragraphs.text: The patient reports an allergy to penicillin, which causes a rash.

paragraphs.label: Family psychiatric history
paragraphs.text: The patient reports his father had bipolar disorder.

paragraphs.label: Relationship / children / living situation
paragraphs.text: The patient is married and has children. The spouse accompanied the patient to the appointment.

The provider recommended starting olanzapine five milligrams at bedtime. It was discussed that weight gain and sleepiness are potential side effects of the medication. The provider also recommended a partial hospitalization program starting Monday, and the alternative of using lithium was discussed.

paragraphs.label: Risks / benefits / alternatives discussed
paragraphs.text: Weight gain and sleepiness as side effects, and the alternative of lithium again were discussed

paragraphs.label: Patient preference / consent / refusal
paragraphs.text: Patient initially refused but consented to try the olanzapine for now
